 News › Learning News › She left NASA, returned to India and cracked UPSC in her fifth attempt: Meet IPS officer Anukriti Sh… She left NASA, returned to India and cracked UPSC in her fifth attempt: Meet IPS officer Anukriti Sharma
 Sajid Raza Updated: Nov 5, 2026, 14:53 IST Meet Anukriti Sharma, Home Minister’s Medal 2026 Awardee Uttar Pradesh IPS officer Anukriti Sharma has been recommended for the prestigious Home Minister's Efficiency Medal 2026. She was one of the officers of the 2020-batch who made headlines when she exposed an insurance fraud of over Rs 100 crore inter-state in Sambhal district.
 Sharma currently serves as Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Women Safety) in Gautam Buddha Nagar. She was later moved from Sambhal to Noida in February, 2026. She hails from Ajmer, Rajasthan and has a strong, sensitive and result-oriented approach towards policing.
 Anukriti Sharma, originally from Ajmer, Rajasthan, embarked on an unusual journey to become an Indian Police Service (IPS) officer. Prior to her career in civil service, she was a scientist in the United States and had the opportunity to work with NASA.
 During her posting in Sambhal, Sharma investigated several cases, including the large-scale insurance fraud that brought her wider recognition.
 Anukriti Sharma's education and research career
 Anukriti Sharma has completed her schooling from Indo-Bharat International School, Jaipur, Rajasthan. She subsequently did her BS-MS from Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER), Kolkata for five years.
 In 2012, she secured admission to a PhD programme at Rice University in Houston, Texas, in the United States. 
 While pursuing her studies for a doctorate degree, she participated in scientific research projects, among them a project dealing with volcanoes.
 Her education also provided her with the chance to work for NASA, the space agency of the United States. She reportedly took home a research stipend of Rs 2 lakh a month.
 Despite having promising opportunities in the field of science and research, Sharma decided to take a different career path. 
 She wanted to do something for the country and take up civil service.
 Anukriti Sharma cleared UPSC in her fifth attempt
 Anukriti Sharma has started her preparation for the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) Civil Services Examination (CSE) from 2014 onwards. In 2015, she took the test for the first time.
 She did not qualify for Mains exam in her first attempt to clear the UPSC Preliminary Examination. She lost the second time when she failed to pass the Prelims.
 However, she continued her preparation and did not give up on her ambition of becoming a civil servant.
 Sharma appeared for the UPSC Civil Services Examination for the fourth time and was able to get the All-India Rank (AIR) 355 in 2018. She was selected for the Indian Revenue Service (IRS) with this rank.
 But it was her plan to get into the Indian Police Service (IPS). She did not want to work for the IRS, so she was going to take the exam again.
 She has worked hard and had her wish of becoming an IPS officer come true in 2020 when she successfully got AIR 138 in UPSC examination.
 Anukriti Sharma's policing career and major achievement
 After joining the IPS, Anukriti Sharma was posted in Uttar Pradesh, where she handled several responsibilities during her service.
 Her investigation of an inter-state insurance fraud worth Rs 100 crore in Sambhal garnered her greater fame. The case involved a large-scale fraud network that was operating from an interstate basis.
 Her involvement in the case and work for policing put her on the national agenda.
 She was transferred to Gautam Buddha Nagar in February, 2026 and posted as Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Women Safety) in the Division.
 Her induction into the Home Minister’s Efficiency Medal 2026 is an acknowledgment of her dedication towards law enforcement.
 The story of Anukriti Sharma from NASA's scientific research to becoming an IPS officer reflects her determination, perseverance and commitment towards public service.
